stem: Read aloud: Lu cannot get the lid off the paint jar. Dan sits at the same table. Mark: listen to three things Lu could say and circle the dots for the one that asks Dan for help (one dot: This lid is stuck. Two dots: Dan, can you help me open it? Three dots: I do not like paint). Spoken, to the day's six: Dan tells Lu how to twist the lid. What does Lu do while Dan talks? The card is invented for practice and the teacher says so aloud.
answer: Two dots, the question. Spoken: Lu listens, waits and looks at Dan. A child may point, act or use a home language.
steps: circles two dots, the asking sentence | says or shows listening, waiting or looking at Dan | the support used is recorded (shown, shown with help, not yet seen)
samples: Two dots; Lu looks at Dan and waits. | One dot, or: I say my idea too.

stem: Hold up Push, Pull, Roll, a book we have not heard yet. Show its front cover, page 2 and its back cover, then read the two credit lines on its title page aloud. Mark: circle the back cover (three pictures: the front cover, page 2, the back cover). Spoken, to the day's six: Who made the pictures in this book?
answer: The back cover. Spoken: the Curio Class art team, the illustrator.
steps: circles the outside back of the book, not page 2 | says the art team or the illustrator made the pictures, or points to the brush label | the support used is recorded
samples: Circles the back cover; the art team made the pictures. | Circles page 2; the writing team made the pictures.
text_ref: front cover, page 2, back cover and the title page credit lines (book not yet heard; day 9 reads it)

stem: Read page 7 of One Hoop, Two Friends aloud again. Mark: circle how the friends will share the hoop (three pictures: the two friends counting to ten with fingers raised; the two friends pulling the hoop between them; Noor walking off with the hoop). Spoken, to the day's six: Ask me one question about what Teo says on this page.
answer: The friends counting to ten. Spoken: a question such as What does Teo say? or Is it Teo's turn next?
steps: circles the counting picture | asks a question about what Teo says, not a statement | the support used is recorded
samples: The counting picture; Is it Teo's turn next? | The pulling picture; Teo is happy.
text_ref: page 7 (the plan to count ten each)

stem: Read page 2 of One Hoop, Two Friends aloud again, its picture covered. Mark: circle the picture that goes with the last sentence (three pictures: Noor running after the rolling hoop; the two friends running to the basket; Teo asking Noor for a turn). Spoken, to the day's six: What could you ask if one word on this page was new to you?
answer: Noor running after the rolling hoop. Spoken: a question about a word, such as What does edge mean? or What does called mean?
steps: circles Noor running after the hoop | asks what a word means, as a question | the support used is recorded
samples: Noor running after the hoop; What does edge mean? | The friends running to the basket; I do not know that word.
text_ref: page 2 (Noor pushes the hoop and runs after it)

stem: Read aloud: Two friends stack cups. One holds the pile steady while the other adds a cup. Mark: circle the picture that belongs in a class message about how these friends play (one child steadying a stack while another adds a cup; a child alone drinking from a cup; two children running). Spoken, to the day's six: Tell me one thing the message could say about these friends. The card is invented for practice and the teacher says so aloud.
answer: The steadying-and-adding picture. Spoken: One holds the cups, or They take turns.
steps: circles the picture of the friends stacking together | says one fact the message could tell | the support used is recorded
samples: The stacking picture; They take turns. | The child drinking alone; I like cups.

stem: Read aloud: Three children open a toy shop. One sorts the toys on a shelf. Draw: in the box on the card, draw a plan picture of one thing a child does in this shop. Spoken, to the day's six: What will a reader learn from your drawing? The card is invented for practice and the teacher says so aloud.
answer: A drawing of a child doing one thing with the toys, such as sorting them on a shelf. Spoken: names the shop and one action, such as One child sorts the toys.
steps: draws a child and the toys doing one thing in the shop | names the shop and one thing that happens in it | the support used is recorded
samples: A child at a shelf of toys; One child sorts the toys. | A toy alone, no child or shop; I like it.

stem: Retry, not scored. Read a new card aloud: Tal offers the drum. Bo asks for a turn. Tal passes it. Mark: circle the picture that matches the last sentence (Tal passing the drum; Tal holding it away; Bo walking off). Spoken, to the day's six: How could a partner ask for help? The card is invented for practice and the teacher says so aloud.
answer: Tal passing the drum. Spoken: Can you help me?
steps: circles the passing picture | asks a question that seeks help | the support used is recorded
samples: The passing picture; Can you help me? | Tal holding it away; I cannot do it.

stem: Read page 6 of Push, Pull, Roll aloud again. Mark: circle the picture that tells what the whole page is about (three pictures: a toy car that goes, stops and turns, with a hand at each step; one toy car standing still; a pole alone). Spoken, to the day's six: Tell me one detail the page gives.
answer: The car that goes, stops and turns. Spoken: a push or a pull can make a toy stop, go faster or slower, or turn a new way.
steps: circles the picture of the whole page, the three steps | gives one detail from page 6 | the support used is recorded
samples: The three steps; it can make a toy stop. | One car standing still; Toys.
text_ref: page 6 (a push or a pull can do more)

stem: Read aloud: The tiny drum is white. The gigantic drum is black. Mark: circle the two drums that fit these words (tiny white and gigantic black; tiny black and gigantic white; two drums the same size). Spoken, to the day's six: Which word tells you which drum is the big one? The card is invented for practice and the teacher says so aloud.
answer: Tiny white and gigantic black. Spoken: gigantic.
steps: circles the tiny white drum and the gigantic black drum | names gigantic as the word for big | the support used is recorded
samples: Tiny white and gigantic black; gigantic. | Tiny black and gigantic white; black.

stem: Read aloud: The page says the pillow and the sock are soft. The shell is hard. The shell goes in another group. Mark: circle the picture of the groups that follows the page (pillow and sock with the shell apart; pillow and shell with the sock apart; all three together). Spoken, to the day's six: What is the rule for the group with the pillow and the sock? The card is invented for practice and the teacher says so aloud.
answer: Pillow and sock together, shell apart. Spoken: soft.
steps: circles the groups that follow the page | names soft as the rule | the support used is recorded
samples: Pillow and sock | shell; soft. | Pillow and shell | sock; They are both red.

stem: Read aloud: The light is on. Now the light is off. Mark: circle the pair of pictures that shows opposites (on and off; on and on; off and off). Spoken, to the day's six, with a tray of sandpaper, smooth paper and a soft cloth: Show me the rough one. The card is invented for practice and the teacher says so aloud.
answer: On and off. Spoken: the child points to the sandpaper.
steps: circles the on and off pair | points to the sandpaper | the support used is recorded
samples: On and off; the sandpaper. | On and on; the smooth paper.

stem: Read aloud: The toy band marches into the hall. The toy cat tiptoes past the dog. Mark: circle the picture that shows how the cat moves (the cat tiptoeing; the cat stomping; the cat marching in a line). Spoken, to the day's six: Show me how the band moves, in a clear space. The card is invented for practice and the teacher says so aloud.
answer: The cat tiptoeing. Spoken: firm, even marching steps, in place or seated with fingers.
steps: circles the tiptoeing cat | shows firm, even steps for the band, different from tiptoeing | the support used is recorded
samples: The tiptoeing cat; heavy even marching. | The marching cat; light tiptoe steps for the band.

stem: Read page 7 of A Toy Can Turn aloud again. Mark: circle the picture that shows what the whole page is about (three pictures: a top and a cart side by side, each turning; a top alone; a cart alone). Spoken, to the day's six: Tell one new detail from this page to add to our topic chart about things that turn.
answer: The top and the cart side by side. Spoken: a detail from page 7, such as A top spins in one place, A cart rolls from place to place, or Each one has something that turns.
steps: circles the picture of both toys | says one detail from page 7 for the topic chart | the support used is recorded
samples: Both toys; A cart rolls from place to place. | The top alone; The top is red.
text_ref: page 7 (a top and a cart: each has something that turns)

stem: Read aloud: The class shelf has a drum and a puzzle. The drum is loud. The puzzle has pieces. Mark: circle the toy you choose for your opinion box (the drum; the puzzle). Spoken, to the day's six: Say your sentence about that toy. The card is invented for practice and the teacher says so aloud.
answer: Either picture, the child's own choice. Spoken: My favorite classroom toy is the, naming the circled toy.
steps: circles one toy | names that toy and says it is a favorite | the support used is recorded
samples: The puzzle; My favorite classroom toy is the puzzle. | The drum; The drum is loud.

stem: Read aloud: The class rocking horse rocks back and forth. It stops by the door. Draw: in the box on the card, draw the horse so your drawing teaches a reader how it moves. Spoken, to the day's six: What will you tell a reader about the horse? The card is invented for practice and the teacher says so aloud.
answer: A drawing of the horse tipped or rocking, with motion lines or arrows. Spoken: It rocks, or It rocks back and forth.
steps: draws the horse showing how it moves | tells one fact about how it moves | the support used is recorded
samples: A horse with rocking lines; It rocks. | A horse with a happy face and no motion; It is a horse.

stem: Retry, not scored. Read a new menu aloud: The shelf has a doll, a puzzle and bells. Mark: circle the toy for your opinion box. Spoken, to the day's six: Say your sentence. The card is invented for practice and the teacher says so aloud.
answer: Any picture. Spoken: My favorite classroom toy is the, naming the circled toy.
steps: circles one toy | names the toy and says it is a favorite | the support used is recorded
samples: The bells; My favorite classroom toy is the bells. | The puzzle; This is a puzzle.

stem: After hearing Folio A once: Ask your partner one question about what Emi requests, then answer your partner's question about a detail. About 2 minutes per group.
answer: A question about Emi's request, such as What does Emi ask for? Answer: to see the puppet.
steps: asks a question about what Emi requests | answers a partner's detail question from the story | the support used is recorded
samples: What does Emi ask for? To see the puppet. | The child tells about a toy at home.
text_ref: whole story

stem: Show the three Folio A pictures. Point to the one that matches Sol lifts the puppet high for Emi, and tell what moment it shows. About 1 minute per group.
answer: The third picture. Spoken: Sol lifts the puppet high for Emi.
steps: points to the third picture | says the moment the picture shows | the support used is recorded
samples: The third picture; Sol lifts the puppet high for Emi. | The first picture, Sol singing.
text_ref: the three pictures and the last sentence

stem: Observed throughout the 8-minute group task on Folio A: follow the agreed listening and turn-taking rules. No added minutes.
answer: Waits, listens and answers the partner's point.
steps: waits for the partner to finish | listens and looks at the partner | takes a turn when it is theirs
samples: Waits, then answers the point the partner made. | Talks over the partner.
text_ref: the group talk about the story

stem: Observed within A1, A5 and A6: keep the puppet talk going for at least two back-and-forth exchanges. No added minutes.
answer: A question, an answer, a related question, an answer.
steps: asks | answers | asks a related question | answers again
samples: Question, answer, What about the song? answer. | One answer, then the child leaves the talk.
text_ref: the group talk about the story

stem: After Folio A: ask for help finding Emi's request, ask what happens next, and ask what lifts means; partners answer in turn. About 3 minutes per group.
answer: Three questions matching their purposes, with relevant answers, such as Where does Emi ask? What happens next? What does lifts mean?
steps: asks for help finding the request | asks what happens next | asks what lifts means
samples: Where does Emi ask? What happens next? What does lifts mean? | I do not know what lifts is.
text_ref: whole story

stem: After hearing Folio A: ask and answer about its key action, and ask for a rereading of one unclear phrase. About 2 minutes per group.
answer: A question about the action with its answer, such as Who lifts the puppet at the end? Sol. Then: Please read after this song again.
steps: asks about the key action | answers from the story | asks for a rereading politely
samples: Who lifts the puppet at the end? Sol. Please read after this song again. | Tells an event that is not in the story.
text_ref: the song sentence and the last sentence

stem: Examine the day 16 drawing and dictated preference, with written teacher feedback already on it. The child revises for 8 minutes today. Keep the piece for day 18; do not score a new day 17 piece.
answer: A named toy and a preference, such as My favorite toy is the top.
steps: a toy is named | a preference is said | revision is made from the feedback
samples: A drawing of a top: My favorite toy is the top. | A drawing of a top: This is a top.

stem: In each group of five children, 2 minutes: share a classroom toy choice while following listening and turn-taking rules.
answer: Listens and takes a turn.
steps: listens while others speak | waits for a turn | speaks when it is the child's turn
samples: Waits, then says a toy choice. | Interrupts a classmate.

stem: In the same groups, 3 minutes: ask, answer and keep talking about toy choices through several exchanges.
answer: Two connected back-and-forth turns, such as a question, an answer, and a related question.
steps: asks about a choice | answers | follows with a related question or answer
samples: Which toy? The puzzle. Why? It has pieces. | One answer, then silence.

stem: Score the day 16 piece revised on day 17, after class (30 teacher minutes). Prompt: name a classroom toy and tell your preference. Score topic and preference separately. Reasons and conventional spelling are not required.
answer: A drawing of a top with My favorite toy is the top, said or dictated.
steps: the topic: a classroom toy is named | the preference: favorite or prefer is said | drawing, dictation or letters all count
samples: A drawing of a top: My favorite toy is the top. | A drawing of a top: This is a top.

stem: Interview a partner about a classroom toy: ask for help, ask for information and ask for clarification, and answer in return. 3 minutes within each six-minute group.
answer: Three questions such as Can you help me pick a toy? What can it do? What do you mean by turn? with relevant answers.
steps: asks for help | asks for information | asks what a word means | answers the partner
samples: Can you help me pick a toy? What can it do? What do you mean by turn? | The child tells a toy fact and asks nothing.

stem: Observed throughout I1 and I3: listening and agreed turns. No added minutes.
answer: Waits and responds to the partner.
steps: waits for the partner | answers the partner's point | takes a turn when it is theirs
samples: Waits, then answers. | Speaks over the partner.

stem: Continue several interview exchanges. 3 minutes within the same group.
answer: Asks, answers and follows with another related question.
steps: asks | answers | follows with a related question
samples: Which toy? The cart. What can it do? It rolls. | One answer, then stops.

stem: Common battery, book kinds, about a quarter of a minute per child: place the familiar story  and a weekly poem beside their type pictures and name each type.
answer: A storybook and a poem.
steps: names the story as a storybook | names the poem as a poem
samples: Storybook; poem. | Calls the poem an information book.
text_ref: the story and a weekly poem

stem: Common battery, story makers, about a quarter of a minute per child: use the actual credits of the story and name its author and illustrator and what each made.
answer: The printed author made the words; the printed illustrator made the pictures.
steps: names the author as the maker of the words | names the illustrator as the maker of the pictures
samples: The author made the words; the illustrator made the pictures. | The roles swapped.
text_ref: the credits page

stem: Common battery, letter names, about a fifth of a minute per child: name A a T t H h P p N n C c scattered on a card. Interim taught subset only.
answer: Names each taught upper- and lowercase form.
steps: names each taught letter in both cases | names, not sounds
samples: All twelve named. | Calls h n, or n h.

stem: Common battery, track, a few seconds per child: follow adult-read Folio C across a line break and a page turn with a finger.
answer: Left to right, the next line below, then the next page.
steps: starts at the left | goes to the next line below | turns to the next page
samples: Finger moves left to right and down. | Starts at the right.
text_ref: both pages

stem: Common battery, letter sequence, a few seconds per child: after hearing pat in Folio C, show pat and tap and ask whether switching the letters keeps the same word. The adult says both spoken words.
answer: No. The order records a different spoken word.
steps: says the word changes | the child need not decode
samples: No, tap is a different word. | The order does not matter.
text_ref: the word pat

stem: Common battery, spaces, about a tenth of a minute per child: box the separate words in I pat my hat from Folio C.
answer: Four boxes, separated at the spaces.
steps: one box for each word | no box around a single letter
samples: Four boxes. | A box around every letter.
text_ref: the first line

stem: Common battery, formation, about a quarter of a minute per child: print A and a from their names without tracing; keep the dated sheets for h, p, n and c. This samples many taught forms, not all.
answer: Recognizable forms in both cases across the record.
steps: prints the uppercase form | prints the lowercase form when asked
samples: A and a both printed. | Only A when a is requested.

stem: Common battery, sound writing, about a quarter of a minute per child: write the letters for the heard short a and the primary sound of t; keep earlier h, p, n and c samples.
answer: The letters a and t.
steps: chooses the letter for the heard sound | then writes it
samples: a for the short a sound; t for /t/. | p for the t sound.

stem: Common battery, consonant sounds, about a fifth of a minute per child: say the primary sounds for printed t, h, p, n and c.
answer: Their taught sounds, with the hard c.
steps: says the sound, not the letter name
samples: Says each sound. | Says the letter name.

stem: Common battery, rhyme, about two fifths of a minute per child: from adult-read Folio C, choose mat or pal to rhyme with pat, then produce another rhyme.
answer: Mat, then hat, bat or another spoken rhyme.
steps: chooses mat | produces a second rhyming word
samples: Mat; then cat. | Pal, because the first sound matches.
text_ref: the rhyming lines

stem: Common battery, syllables, about two fifths of a minute per child: say puppet, count and segment its syllables, then blend the spoken parts wag and on. No print.
answer: Puppet; two; pup, pet; wagon.
steps: counts two beats | splits pup, pet | blends wagon
samples: Two; pup, pet; wagon. | Counts the separate sounds in puppet.

stem: Common battery, mapped words, about a third of a minute per child: read I, my, me, the and a in shuffled order and at their places in Folio C. The adult reads other words without cueing these five.
answer: Reads the five taught words in both settings.
steps: reads each word in the shuffled list | reads it again in the poem
samples: All five in both settings. | Guesses a word from a picture.
text_ref: I, my, the, a in the lines

stem: Common battery, book parts, about a quarter of a minute per child: on the information book Push, Pull, Roll, show the front cover, back cover and title page.
answer: Points to all three.
steps: points to the front cover | points to the back cover | points to the title page
samples: All three shown. | Chooses the last page as the back cover.
text_ref: the covers and title page

stem: Common battery, information makers, about a quarter of a minute per child: on Push, Pull, Roll, name the credited author and illustrator and what each made.
answer: Both credited names; words and pictures respectively.
steps: names the author for the words | names the illustrator for the pictures
samples: The author wrote the words; the illustrator made the pictures. | The roles swapped.
text_ref: the credits

stem: Score the day 27 toy portrait after class (30 teacher minutes), carrying the written feedback from after day 27 and the revision on day 29. Score a named topic and accurate information separately.
answer: Our classmate prefers the cart. Its wheels roll, with a matching drawing and a source detail from the information books.
steps: a classmate's toy is named | one accurate fact | matches the drawing
samples: Our classmate prefers the cart. Its wheels roll. | I like it.
text_ref: a detail of the child's toy

stem: Hear Folio B whole. Name its main topic and retell two details. 1 minute per group.
answer: Bouncing toys; a ball bounces up, a spring toy goes up and down.
steps: names the topic: bouncing toys | retells two details
samples: Bouncing toys; the ball, the spring toy. | The bean bag as the topic.
text_ref: whole booklet

stem: Ask a detail question and answer a partner using Folio B. 1 minute per group.
answer: A question and its answer, such as What stays on the floor? The bean bag.
steps: asks a detail question | answers from the book
samples: What stays on the floor? The bean bag. | A fact about a toy that is not in the book.
text_ref: the bean bag page

stem: Choose the pictured action that matches A ball falls to the floor and bounces up, and explain how it matches the words. 1 minute per group.
answer: The picture of the ball going down, then up.
steps: chooses the down-and-up picture | says falls and bounces up match it
samples: The ball goes down, then up. | The ball only goes down.
text_ref: page 1 and its picture

stem: Confirm the spring toy's movement from the book read aloud with a question and answer, and ask for clarification of an unclear phrase. 1 minute per group.
answer: Does the spring toy go up and down? Yes. Please read bounces up and down again.
steps: asks about the movement | answers | asks for a rereading
samples: Does the spring toy go up and down? Yes; please read bounces up and down again. | Guesses a movement the book did not say.
text_ref: the spring toy page

stem: Sort a fresh set of long and short toy pictures by length only and say the rule. three quarters of a minute per group.
answer: Consistent length groups, and the rule named: long and short.
steps: groups by length only | names the rule
samples: Long here, short there; length. | Mixes color with length.

stem: Pair wet with dry and loud with quiet, then say the opposite of a new verb card, stop. three quarters of a minute per group.
answer: wet and dry; loud and quiet; go for stop.
steps: wet with dry | loud with quiet | go for stop
samples: All three pairs. | Wet with soaked; or stop repeated for stop.

stem: Choose the new word card shiny and connect it to a real classroom object. half a minute per group.
answer: The bell is shiny.
steps: chooses shiny | links it to an object that fits
samples: The bell is shiny. | Calls a dull block shiny.

stem: Act out hop, creep and stomp (new verbs), in a clear space; seated finger movements are acceptable. 1 minute per group.
answer: Light springs; slow, low steps; heavy, flat steps.
steps: three movements that differ | each fits its word
samples: Three different movements. | All three done the same way.

stem: During V1 to V4, use a learned word on its own. No added minutes.
answer: This toy feels smooth.
steps: uses a learned word | the word fits the object
samples: This toy feels smooth. | Says smooth about a rough object.

stem: During shared reading of the story and the poems, join a purposeful return and give one detail linked to the text. half a minute per group.
answer: Joins the poem and finds a story moment.
steps: joins the poem | points to or tells a story moment
samples: Joins the poem and points to a moment. | Tells a story that is not the text.
text_ref: the story and the poem p07

stem: During reading of the page Attributes of Toys, join and point to a describing word on the page and use it. half a minute per group.
answer: Points to a describing word and uses it.
steps: points to a describing word | uses the word
samples: Points to tiny and says The bead is tiny. | Supplies an unrelated word.
text_ref: the describing words

stem: Components first taught on day 28, at most 1 minute per child within 30 foundations minutes: name M m R r, print their uppercase and lowercase forms, write m and r for the heard primary sounds, say the sounds from the letters, then read in alone and within the new adult-read sentence The cart is in the box. Keep any matching dated observation from days 29 to 31; collect only the missing parts.
answer: Both names and sounds, four recognizable forms, matching sound spellings, and in in both settings.
steps: names M m R r | prints four forms | writes m and r for the sounds | says the sounds | reads in both ways
samples: Names, prints and sounds all four. | Calls m n.

stem: Say the whole word from the spoken parts s and un; then split the spoken word fish into its first sound and the rest. half a minute per child, 15 foundations minutes, fresh oral words never taught. No print.
answer: Sun; f and ish.
steps: blends s and un into sun | splits fish into f and ish
samples: Sun; f, ish. | Leaves s and un apart; splits fish into f, i, sh.

stem: The same interview as I1 for the remaining children: ask a partner for help, information and clarification about a classroom toy, and answer in return. Three minutes within each group. Do not repeat a child already recorded.
answer: Three questions such as Can you help me pick a toy? What can it do? What do you mean by turn? with relevant answers.
steps: asks for help | asks for information | asks what a word means | answers the partner
samples: Can you help me pick a toy? What can it do? What do you mean by turn? | The child tells a toy fact and asks nothing.

stem: The same observation as I2 for the remaining children, throughout the interviews. No added minutes.
answer: Waits and responds to the partner.
steps: waits for the partner | answers the partner's point | takes a turn when it is theirs
samples: Waits, then answers. | Speaks over the partner.

stem: The same observation as I3 for the remaining children: several interview exchanges. Three minutes within the group.
answer: Asks, answers and follows with another related question.
steps: asks | answers | follows with a related question
samples: Which toy? The cart. What can it do? It rolls. | One answer, then stops.

stem: Read page 8 of Mira Makes a Road aloud again. Mark: circle what Mira does when Kiko comes (three pictures: Mira and Kiko with the toy lion on her road; Mira playing zoo with the group; Mira pushing the lion away). Spoken, to the day's six: Ask me a question about what the words on this page show about Mira.
answer: Mira and Kiko with the lion on the road. Spoken: a question about Mira from the page, such as Why does Mira let Kiko play? or How does Mira feel when Kiko likes her road?
steps: circles Mira and Kiko with the lion on the road | asks a question about what Mira does, says or feels on the page | the support used is recorded
samples: Mira and Kiko with the lion; Why does Mira let Kiko play? | The zoo game; Mira is nice.
text_ref: page 8 (Kiko comes to Mira's road)

stem: Read page 3 of Mira Makes a Road aloud again. Mark: circle the picture for the last sentence (three pictures: Mira lying by her road, tongue poking out, thinking; the road going past the chair with no one there; Mira standing at the block shelf). Spoken, to the day's six: Which words go with your picture?
answer: Mira with her tongue poking out. Spoken: her tongue poked out, or thinking hard.
steps: circles Mira with her tongue poking out | says the words that go with the picture | the support used is recorded
samples: Mira thinking; her tongue poked out. | The road past the chair; Mira is crying.

stem: Read page 9 of Mira Makes a Road aloud again. Mark: circle where Mira chooses to stay (three pictures: Mira laying a new block at the end of her road; Mira with the zoo group; Mira at the door). Spoken, to the day's six: Which words tell you Mira still likes her road?
answer: Mira laying a new block at the end of her road. Spoken: she hummed her tune, or she began a new bit at the end.
steps: circles Mira at the end of her road | gives words such as she hummed her tune or began a new bit, or points to them on the page | the support used is recorded

stem: Read page 8 of The Magic Bow aloud again. Mark: circle the picture that shows the people after the story turns (three pictures: a child stacking blocks while a friend points to help; the people with their heads down; the empty stool). Spoken, to the day's six: What do the people do now that the bow is gone?
answer: The child stacking blocks with a friend helping. Spoken: they keep on trying, or they ask each other for help.
steps: circles the child stacking blocks with a friend | says they keep trying or ask each other for help | the support used is recorded
samples: The blocks and the friend; they keep trying. | The people with heads down; they get the bow back.
text_ref: page 8 (the people keep trying)

stem: Read two cards aloud: Mo sends a ball down a ramp. Lee waits by the ramp for a turn. Mark: circle the one picture that fits both cards (three pictures: Mo and Lee both rolling balls; Mo rolling a ball down a ramp with Lee waiting beside it; a ball alone on the floor).
